card_product.point_value_baseline_basis: IndiGo BluChips have no stated rupee value (re-checked 2026-11-07, W9). Axis T&C (IndiGo BluChip Program Specific Terms 1): "loyalty points and do not hold any monetary value", not legal tender, cannot be exchanged for cash; Axis T&C earn clause: "The bank has no role in determining the validity or the redemption value of the IndiGo BluChips". eligibility_engine.notes: Axis page: primary cardholder 18 to 70, resident of India. KVB's wording for its premium cards ("Earn 2 Reward Points for every Rs 100 spent, plus 3X points on flights...") shows the multiplier can be read as extra points on top of the base, so the reading is genuinely ambiguous.
Categories that earn no points, any monthly or annual points cap, rounding and the minimum transaction are not stated.

First-year annual fee: the March 2025 MITC said "Waived for 1st year"; the August 2026 KFS cum MITC and the card page list joining fee nil and annual fee ₹999 with a waiver from the 2nd year on spend. Whether the first-year fee is billed needs a person to confirm; the 2026 documents are followed.

Cash withdrawal fee conflict: the KFS cum MITC says ₹300 per transaction or 1% of the amount, whichever is higher; the card page says 2% of the cash withdrawn or ₹300, whichever is higher. The MITC value (1%) is used.
Redemption conflict: the KFS cum MITC says a minimum of 800 points for later redemptions; the card page says 250. Both agree on 2,000 points for the first redemption and a ₹99 fee per request.

Add-on card fee: the card page says "Free"; the March 2025 MITC said ₹200 for retail add-on cards; the 2026 MITC has no add-on fee column. Free is used; the maximum number of add-on cards is not stated.

The KFS cum MITC says the retail annual-fee waiver spend counts "retail spends other than cash withdrawal in the previous year" and its note excludes fuel, instalments, fees, charges, GST, cash withdrawals and reversals; the period is read as the card anniversary year.

KVB also sells Oura (Visa Platinum, ₹2,999), Samara (Visa Signature, ₹5,999), Alturas and Eternis (Visa Infinite, ₹14,999 and ₹29,999) and Visa-network corporate cards, and a co-branded KVB SBI card; none is in the candidate list, and Oura and Samara are also described as Visa Platinum and Visa Signature, so they must not be confused with these two cards.
Merchant offers on the retail offers page are dated Visa coupons (many ended before 7 Nov 2026) and are not modelled.

Lounge access: the page says only "4 Complimentary Airport lounge access within India"; the period (per year, half-year or quarter), spend criteria and lounge list are not stated anywhere, so quota_period is N/A.
notes: Interest 3.25% a month (39% a year) on purchases and cash advances; interest-free period 15 to 45 days on retail purchases when the previous balance is paid in full (MITC). Payment due dates are the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th or 25th; billing date is 15 days before the due date.

Fuel surcharge 1%, waived for single transactions of ₹500 to ₹4,000, maximum ₹200 per billing cycle (MITC and page). Forex 3.5%. Card replacement ₹199 (waived for fraud or reissue on expiry). Fee on cash payment at a branch ₹100. Cash advance limit 40% of the credit limit.

EMI conversion from ₹500 at 15% to 22% depending on vintage and balance transfer from ₹10,000 at 18% (page); EMI or BT processing ₹300 or 1% of the loan, whichever is higher, and 3% foreclosure (MITC).

T&C 3.4(d) lists categories that are "not eligible to earn", which implies other spend might earn, but no rate is printed. base_points_per_block and the return percent are left null and no non-travel earn rule is drafted. Action: ask RBL in writing (cardservices@rbl.bank.in, toll free 1800 102 6222) whether everyday non-travel spend earns points and at what rate, or have the product owner decide to publish the card as travel-only earn.

open_questions: HELD: no reward rate for the current card is published. Re-read in wave 3 (W11, 2026-11-07): the product page, its Top Benefits slider (earn cashbacks, works everywhere, 1-click controls on the app, scan and pay for UPI: all images with headline text only), the What-comes-with-the-card items (lifetime free, works everywhere, 1% fuel surcharge waiver, lounge), the 7 FAQs, the usage guide, MITC V18 (the "English" MITC link on the page resolves to it; no Zagg or Rio coin terms in it) and the Cardmember Agreement state no cashback or coin rate. The only rate is the footnote for cards issued before 10 Jan 2025 (0.5 Rio coins per ₹50 on non-UPI and 1.5 Rio coins per ₹50 on UPI, outside exclusion categories). The page says any programme run by the Zagg app is the app provider's sole responsibility, so the current cashback programme sits outside YES documents. The value of a Rio coin is not stated. No reward rules are written. To unblock: ask YES BANK or Zagg for the Zagg card rewards terms.

Network (settled 2026-11-07, W11): RuPay, from card art on YES BANK's own Zagg pages (the usage guide PDF, the hero banner and the Top Benefits slide all show "YES BANK" and the RuPay logo). The product FAQ also says the card links to UPI apps ("NPCI recognised TPAPs"). The MITC and KFS do not name the network.

RIO and Zagg: the issuer lists one product. The page assets are named "rio_*" and the pre-10-Jan-2025 footnote speaks of Rio coins, so Rio is the earlier name of the same card; the old co-brand MITC (undated Mizo translation) lists "Rio" and the current MITC lists "Zagg". Treated as one card.
Lounge: two domestic visits a calendar quarter (page, listing) with a ₹50,000 prior-quarter spend condition (MITC 3(r), Lounge Program). Whether any international lounge access exists is not stated.
Fuel surcharge waiver: from 15 Jun 2026 ₹400 to ₹5,000 and ₹250 per statement cycle (MITC 4, KFS); the page glossary says the cap is ₹250 and states no range. No waiver on UPI fuel transactions.
notes: Forex mark-up is 3.50% (MITC and KFS list Zagg with BYOC / EMI / Wellness / Novio / Max).
The Zagg usage guide PDF is a single image page with no extractable text.

value.rule: 10% of the statement balance or ₹1,350, whichever is lower, per statement; nothing if the current outstanding (statement balance + unbilled) is ₹500 or less
value.note: A percentage fee cannot be written as fixed slabs, so late_payment_slabs is empty.

rules: Late payment charge: no charge if the current outstanding (statement balance + unbilled) is up to ₹500; above ₹500, 10% of the statement balance or ₹1,350, whichever is lower, per statement (MITC 3(b), KFS).

Auto-debit / payment return failure: from 15 Jun 2026, 2.5% or ₹500 whichever is higher on the net payable amount, capped at ₹5,000 per customer per statement (before that 2% or ₹450, cap ₹1,500); cheque return ₹450 (MITC 3(d)).
Overlimit: ₹550 + GST per transaction that exceeds the limit (facility reintroduced 1 Jun 2026) (MITC 3(c)).

Cash advance: from 15 Jun 2026, 2.5% or ₹650 whichever is higher; before that 2.5% or ₹500; not applicable to virtual cards; cash withdrawal suspended for the first 6 months after onboarding; limit up to 30% of the credit limit (MITC 3(a), 5).
